report.answer_text:
On October 22, 2025, Google reported that its Willow quantum chip ran an algorithm called Quantum Echoes in about two hours. Google estimated that the best known classical method would take 13,000 times as long on one of the world’s fastest supercomputers. The results were published in *Nature*. (research.google)
Google called it the first verifiable quantum advantage: a comparably capable quantum computer could repeat the calculation and check the result. The speedup was for one specific task—measuring how a disturbance spreads through a quantum system—not a claim that Willow is faster than supercomputers at everything. Google also reported a separate proof-of-concept experiment using the technique to study molecular structure. (blog.google)

quotes.text: In a separate, proof-of-principle experiment Quantum computation of molecular geometry via many-body nuclear spin echoes (to be posted on arXiv later today), we showed how our new technique — a “molecular ruler” — can measure longer distances than today’s methods, using data from Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) to gain more information about chemical structure.

In a proof-of-principle experiment in partnership with The University of California, Berkeley, we ran the Quantum Echoes algorithm on our Willow chip to study two molecules, one with 15 atoms and another with 28 atoms, to verify this approach.
